parts.title: Part A
parts.instructions: Escucha la conversación y elige la respuesta que mejor responde a la pregunta. Suena una sola vez.

script.speaker: Man
script.text: Did you get tickets for the concert?

script.speaker: Woman
script.text: They sold out before I even opened the page.

questions.stem: What does the woman mean?
questions.explanation: «Sold out» antes de que pudiera intentarlo.

script.speaker: Woman
script.text: Is the deadline negotiable?

script.speaker: Man
script.text: That is set in stone.

questions.stem: What does the man mean?
questions.explanation: «Set in stone» = inamovible.

script.speaker: Man
script.text: How was your first week?

script.speaker: Woman
script.text: I am still finding my feet.

questions.stem: What does the woman mean?
questions.explanation: «Find one's feet» = irse adaptando.

script.speaker: Woman
script.text: Should I mention the error in the meeting?

script.speaker: Man
script.text: I would raise it privately first.

questions.stem: What does the man advise?
questions.explanation: «Raise it privately» = plantearlo en privado.

script.speaker: Man
script.text: The software update broke everything.

script.speaker: Woman
script.text: You are not the only one.

questions.stem: What does the woman mean?
questions.explanation: «You are not the only one» = le pasa a más gente.

script.speaker: Woman
script.text: Do you want to lead the presentation?

script.speaker: Man
script.text: I would rather support than lead this time.

questions.stem: What will the man do?
questions.explanation: «Would rather X than Y» expresa preferencia clara.

script.speaker: Man
script.text: Have you decided on a topic?

script.speaker: Woman
script.text: I have narrowed it down to two.

questions.stem: What does the woman mean?
questions.explanation: «Narrow down» = reducir opciones.

script.speaker: Woman
script.text: Was the trip worth it?

script.speaker: Man
script.text: Every penny.

questions.stem: What does the man mean?
questions.explanation: «Every penny» confirma que valió lo que costó.

script.speaker: Man
script.text: Can I borrow your notes from Tuesday?

script.speaker: Woman
script.text: I was not there either.

questions.stem: What does the woman mean?
questions.explanation: «Either» revela que ella tampoco fue.

script.speaker: Woman
script.text: The committee rejected it again.

script.speaker: Man
script.text: Third time is the charm, they say.

questions.stem: What does the man imply?
options: He hopes the next attempt succeeds.
questions.explanation: Ironía optimista: a la tercera va la vencida.

script.speaker: Man
script.text: Is the fee refundable?

script.speaker: Woman
script.text: Only up to a week before.

questions.stem: What does the woman mean?
options: It is refundable if cancelled early enough.
questions.explanation: Hay plazo: hasta una semana antes.

script.speaker: Woman
script.text: You look exhausted.

script.speaker: Man
script.text: I have been burning the midnight oil.

questions.stem: What does the man mean?
questions.explanation: «Burn the midnight oil» = trasnochar trabajando.

script.speaker: Man
script.text: Do you agree with her conclusion?

script.speaker: Woman
script.text: Up to a point.

questions.stem: What does the woman mean?
questions.explanation: «Up to a point» = hasta cierto punto.

script.speaker: Woman
script.text: Did the funding come through?

script.speaker: Man
script.text: Not yet, and I am not holding my breath.

questions.stem: What does the man mean?
questions.explanation: «Not holding my breath» = no espero que pase.

script.speaker: Man
script.text: Was the criticism fair?

script.speaker: Woman
script.text: It stung, but yes.

questions.stem: What does the woman mean?
questions.explanation: «It stung» = dolió, pero admite que era justa.

script.speaker: Woman
script.text: Shall I book the small room?

script.speaker: Man
script.text: Better make it the large one.

questions.stem: What does the man suggest?
questions.explanation: «Better make it» propone cambiar a la grande.

script.speaker: Man
script.text: How is the group project going?

script.speaker: Woman
script.text: Let us just say I am doing most of it.

questions.stem: What does the woman imply?
questions.explanation: Queja indirecta: hace la mayor parte.

script.speaker: Woman
script.text: Do we have enough copies?

script.speaker: Man
script.text: Just about.

questions.stem: What does the man mean?
questions.explanation: «Just about» = justo, por los pelos.

script.speaker: Man
script.text: Are you going to challenge the grade?

script.speaker: Woman
script.text: It is not worth the trouble.

questions.stem: What will the woman do?
questions.explanation: «Not worth the trouble» = no merece el esfuerzo.

script.speaker: Woman
script.text: Is the machine reliable?

script.speaker: Man
script.text: It has never let me down.

questions.stem: What does the man mean?
questions.explanation: «Let someone down» = fallar a alguien.

script.speaker: Man
script.text: Did you understand the last section?

script.speaker: Woman
script.text: It went right over my head.

questions.stem: What does the woman mean?
questions.explanation: «Go over one's head» = no entender nada.

script.speaker: Woman
script.text: Are you sure about the figures?

script.speaker: Man
script.text: I double-checked them twice.

questions.stem: What does the man mean?
questions.explanation: Los comprobó repetidamente.

script.speaker: Man
script.text: The train is delayed forty minutes.

script.speaker: Woman
script.text: Of course it is.

questions.stem: What does the woman's tone suggest?
questions.explanation: «Of course it is» dicho así expresa hartazgo, no acuerdo.

script.speaker: Woman
script.text: Should we include the pilot data?

script.speaker: Man
script.text: I would leave it out.

questions.stem: What does the man advise?
questions.explanation: «Leave it out» = dejarlo fuera.

script.speaker: Man
script.text: Is she coming back to the department?

script.speaker: Woman
script.text: That ship has sailed.

questions.stem: What does the woman mean?
questions.explanation: «That ship has sailed» = ya pasó el momento.

script.speaker: Woman
script.text: Do you want me to explain it again?

script.speaker: Man
script.text: Please, if you do not mind.

questions.stem: What does the man want?
questions.explanation: Acepta cortésmente.

script.speaker: Man
script.text: The results are inconclusive.

script.speaker: Woman
script.text: Which is a result in itself.

questions.stem: What does the woman mean?
questions.explanation: Que no concluya también dice algo.

script.speaker: Woman
script.text: Have you spoken to your advisor about it?

script.speaker: Man
script.text: I keep meaning to.

questions.stem: What does the man mean?
options: He intends to but has not.
questions.explanation: «Keep meaning to» = lo pienso hacer y lo voy dejando.

script.speaker: Man
script.text: Is this the final version?

script.speaker: Woman
script.text: Give or take a few commas.

questions.stem: What does the woman mean?
questions.explanation: «Give or take» = con pequeñas diferencias.

script.speaker: Woman
script.text: Did the professor like your proposal?

script.speaker: Man
script.text: She had a lot of questions.

questions.stem: What can be inferred?
questions.explanation: Muchas preguntas sugiere reservas, no entusiasmo.

parts.title: Part B · Conversación 1
parts.instructions: Escucha la conversación y responde a las preguntas. Suena una sola vez.

script.speaker: Student
script.text: I am trying to book the recording studio for my final project, but everything is taken.

script.speaker: Technician
script.text: Final projects always land in the same three weeks. How long do you need?

script.speaker: Student
script.text: Six hours, ideally in one session.

script.speaker: Technician
script.text: Six consecutive hours will not happen this month. What I can offer is two three-hour blocks.

script.speaker: Student
script.text: Would I have to set everything up twice?

script.speaker: Technician
script.text: Normally yes, but if both blocks are on the same day I can leave your configuration saved.

script.speaker: Student
script.text: That would save nearly an hour.

script.speaker: Technician
script.text: There is a morning and an evening block free on the twelfth. The gap is four hours.

script.speaker: Student
script.text: I can work on the edit during the gap. Let us take it.

script.speaker: Technician
script.text: Booked. Bring your own cables; ours have been going missing.

questions.stem: What does the student need?
questions.explanation: Lo dice al principio.

questions.stem: Why is the studio so busy?
options: Final projects fall in the same weeks.
questions.explanation: Explicación del técnico.

questions.stem: What is the advantage of booking both blocks on the same day?
options: The configuration can be left saved.
questions.explanation: Ahorra montar dos veces.

questions.stem: What does the technician ask the student to bring?
questions.explanation: Última intervención.

parts.title: Part B · Conversación 2
parts.instructions: Escucha la conversación y responde a las preguntas. Suena una sola vez.

script.speaker: Woman
script.text: Your draft argues that the decline began in 1870. The sources you cite say 1890.

script.speaker: Man
script.text: The 1890 figure is when the decline was first recorded, not when it started.

script.speaker: Woman
script.text: That is an important distinction, but it is not in the text.

script.speaker: Man
script.text: I thought it was implied by the paragraph on record-keeping.

script.speaker: Woman
script.text: Implied is not enough for a claim that carries the whole chapter.

script.speaker: Man
script.text: So I should state it explicitly and defend it.

script.speaker: Woman
script.text: State it, defend it, and anticipate the objection that absence of records is not evidence of absence.

script.speaker: Man
script.text: There is a parish census from 1875 that supports me.

script.speaker: Woman
script.text: Then that census belongs in the main argument, not in a footnote where you have it now.

script.speaker: Man
script.text: Understood. It is the strongest thing I have and I buried it.

questions.stem: What is the main problem with the draft?
options: A key distinction is not stated explicitly.
questions.explanation: La distinción entre inicio y registro no aparece en el texto.

questions.stem: What does 1890 represent, according to the man?
options: When the decline was first recorded.
questions.explanation: Su respuesta inicial.

questions.stem: What objection must the man anticipate?
options: That absence of records is not evidence of absence.
That the census is a forgery.
That the chapter is too short.
questions.explanation: Lo dice la supervisora textualmente.

questions.stem: What does the woman say about the 1875 census?
options: It should move from the footnote to the main argument.
questions.explanation: Está enterrado en una nota y es lo más fuerte que tiene.

parts.title: Part C · Charla 1
parts.instructions: Escucha la charla y responde a las preguntas. Suena una sola vez.

script.speaker: Professor
script.text: Standard time zones did not exist before the railways, and it is worth understanding why they became necessary.

script.speaker: Professor
script.text: Until the middle of the nineteenth century, each town kept its own time, set by the sun at noon. A town fifteen miles east was a minute ahead, and nobody was inconvenienced.

script.speaker: Professor
script.text: Railways changed that, not because trains were fast, but because timetables have to be shared.

script.speaker: Professor
script.text: A single printed timetable covering fifty towns with fifty local times is not a timetable; it is a puzzle.

script.speaker: Professor
script.text: The companies imposed their own standard first, and governments followed years later. In several countries the legal adoption of standard time came decades after everyone was already using it.

script.speaker: Professor
script.text: That order matters. The law did not create the standard. It recognised one that commerce had already established.

questions.stem: What is the main point of the talk?
options: Trains became faster in the nineteenth century.
Shared timetables made standard time necessary.
questions.explanation: Es el argumento central.

questions.stem: How was time set before the railways?
options: By the sun at noon in each town.
questions.explanation: Segundo párrafo.

questions.stem: Why does the professor say trains' speed was not the reason?
questions.explanation: «not because trains were fast, but because timetables have to be shared».

questions.stem: What does the professor emphasise about the legal adoption?
options: It followed a standard already in use.
questions.explanation: Última frase de la charla.

parts.title: Part C · Charla 2
parts.instructions: Escucha la charla y responde a las preguntas. Suena una sola vez.

script.speaker: Researcher
script.text: I want to describe an experiment with crows that is often reported inaccurately.

script.speaker: Researcher
script.text: The birds were shown a tube containing water with food floating out of reach, and stones beside it.

script.speaker: Researcher
script.text: Several dropped stones into the tube until the water rose enough to reach the food.

script.speaker: Researcher
script.text: The popular account says this proves the crows understood displacement, and that is a stronger claim than the data supports.

script.speaker: Researcher
script.text: What the experiment shows is that they solved the problem. Whether they reasoned about volume or simply learned that dropping stones brings food closer is not distinguishable from the results.

script.speaker: Researcher
script.text: A follow-up used sawdust instead of water. Birds that had learned the trick kept dropping stones into the sawdust, where it does nothing. That is evidence against the deeper understanding.

questions.stem: What did the crows do in the original experiment?
options: Waited for the food to sink.
Dropped stones to raise the water.
questions.explanation: Tercera intervención.

questions.stem: What claim does the researcher consider too strong?
options: That crows learn from each other.
questions.explanation: Lo dice explícitamente.

questions.stem: What was used in the follow-up experiment?
questions.explanation: Serrín, donde las piedras no elevan nada.

questions.stem: What did the follow-up suggest?
options: The crows had learned a routine, not a principle.
questions.explanation: Siguieron echando piedras donde no servía.

parts.title: Part C · Charla 3
parts.instructions: Escucha el anuncio y responde a las preguntas. Suena una sola vez.

script.speaker: Announcer
script.text: A notice for everyone using the main reading room this month.

script.speaker: Announcer
script.text: The ceiling repairs will begin on the fifteenth and are expected to last three weeks.

script.speaker: Announcer
script.text: During that period the reading room will close, but the collections remain available through the request desk on the ground floor.

script.speaker: Announcer
script.text: Requests placed before noon will be ready the same afternoon; those placed later will be ready the next morning.

script.speaker: Announcer
script.text: Group study rooms on the second floor are unaffected and can still be booked online as usual.

questions.stem: Why will the reading room close?
questions.explanation: Segunda frase.

questions.stem: How long are the works expected to last?
questions.explanation: Dato explícito.

questions.stem: When will a request placed at two in the afternoon be ready?
questions.explanation: Después del mediodía, al día siguiente.

questions.stem: What remains unaffected?
questions.explanation: Última frase.

parts.title: Structure
parts.instructions: Elige la palabra o frase que completa correctamente la oración.

questions.stem: ______ the committee approved the budget did the work begin.
questions.explanation: «Only after» al principio fuerza la inversión que ya trae la frase («did the work begin»).

questions.stem: The species is remarkable for its ability ______ in near-total darkness.
questions.explanation: «Ability» va seguido de infinitivo: the ability to do something.

questions.stem: Were the funding available, the team ______ the study next year.
questions.explanation: Condicional invertido irreal («Were the funding available» = If the funding were available) exige «would».

questions.stem: The results, ______ surprising, were confirmed by two other laboratories.
questions.explanation: «While surprising» = aunque sorprendentes. Es una reducción admitida; las otras no encajan.

questions.stem: Neither the report nor the appendices ______ the raw data.
questions.explanation: Con «neither... nor» concuerda con el sujeto más cercano: «the appendices», plural.

questions.stem: It was not until 1958 ______ the theory was widely accepted.
questions.explanation: Construcción enfática «It was not until X that Y».

questions.stem: The more carefully the samples are stored, ______.
questions.explanation: Doble comparativo: «the more..., the more...». Ambas mitades llevan «the».

questions.stem: Scarcely ______ the lecture begun when the fire alarm sounded.
questions.explanation: «Scarcely... when» con pasado perfecto invertido: «Scarcely had the lecture begun».

questions.stem: The museum houses artefacts ______ origins remain disputed.
questions.explanation: «Whose» expresa posesión y sirve también para cosas.

questions.stem: The regulation applies to all employees, ______ of length of service.
questions.explanation: «Regardless of» = independientemente de.

questions.stem: Rather than ______ the experiment, the team revised the method.
questions.explanation: «Rather than» se empareja con la forma del otro verbo: «revised» → base «abandon».

questions.stem: The instrument is sensitive enough ______ changes of one microgram.
questions.explanation: «Enough to + infinitivo».

questions.stem: Such ______ the demand that the edition sold out in a week.
questions.explanation: Inversión tras «such»: «Such was the demand that...».

questions.stem: The author, ______ work influenced a generation, died in obscurity.
questions.explanation: «Whose work» expresa posesión: su obra.

questions.stem: No sooner had the results appeared ______ they were challenged.
questions.explanation: «No sooner... than». Emparejarlo con «when» es el error clásico.

parts.title: Written Expression
parts.instructions: Señala el fragmento subrayado que NO es correcto.

questions.stem: (A) The number of species (B) recorded in the survey (C) have increased (D) every year since 2010.
questions.explanation: «The number of» va en singular: has increased.

questions.stem: (A) She is accustomed (B) to work (C) under pressure, (D) which helps in this role.
questions.explanation: «Accustomed to» va con gerundio: to working.

questions.stem: (A) The experiment failed (B) because of (C) the temperature was (D) not properly controlled.
questions.explanation: «Because of» va con sustantivo; con oración va «because».

questions.stem: (A) Hardly nobody (B) attended the session, (C) which was scheduled (D) during the holiday.
questions.explanation: Doble negación: «hardly anybody», no «hardly nobody».

questions.stem: (A) The findings apply (B) to adults, (C) to adolescents and (D) children as well.
questions.explanation: Paralelismo: debería ser «to children as well».

questions.stem: (A) A large amount of (B) participants (C) withdrew before (D) the second session.
questions.explanation: Con contables va «number»: a large number of participants.

questions.stem: (A) The professor made (B) us to repeat (C) the procedure (D) three times.
questions.explanation: «Make» va con infinitivo sin «to»: made us repeat.

questions.stem: (A) This method is (B) superior than (C) the one described (D) in the earlier study.
questions.explanation: «Superior to», no «superior than».

questions.stem: (A) The data suggests (B) that the effect (C) is more stronger (D) at higher altitudes.
questions.explanation: «Stronger» ya es comparativo: sobra «more».

questions.stem: (A) Having finished the analysis, (B) the report (C) was written (D) in two days.
questions.explanation: Participio colgante: quien terminó el análisis no fue el informe. El sujeto debería ser una persona.

questions.stem: (A) The technique works well (B) in theory, (C) but in practice it (D) rarely never succeeds.
questions.explanation: «Rarely» y «never» juntos son doble negación.

questions.stem: (A) Each of the three (B) hypotheses (C) have been (D) tested independently.
questions.explanation: «Each of» va en singular: has been.

questions.stem: (A) The library has (B) fewer books (C) than before, (D) but more informations online.
questions.explanation: «Information» es incontable: no admite plural.

questions.stem: (A) He recommended (B) me to apply (C) before the (D) end of the month.
questions.explanation: «Recommend» no admite «recommend somebody to do»: «recommended that I apply».

questions.stem: (A) The two versions (B) of the manuscript (C) differ from (D) very little.
questions.explanation: «Differ» aquí no lleva preposición: «differ very little».

questions.stem: (A) Not only the cost (B) but also the delay (C) were unacceptable (D) to the client.
questions.explanation: Con «not only... but also» concuerda con el sujeto más cercano: «the delay», singular.

questions.stem: (A) The building was (B) design by an architect (C) who never saw (D) it completed.
questions.explanation: Pasiva con participio: was designed.

questions.stem: (A) There has been (B) many attempts (C) to replicate (D) the original result.
questions.explanation: El sujeto es «many attempts», plural: there have been.

questions.stem: (A) The results were (B) discussed (C) between the five (D) members of the panel.
questions.explanation: Con más de dos se usa «among»: among the five members.

questions.stem: (A) Despite that (B) the sample was small, (C) the conclusions (D) were widely reported.
questions.explanation: «Despite» no introduce oración: debería ser «Although».

questions.stem: (A) The team spent (B) three months (C) to collect (D) the field data.
questions.explanation: «Spend time doing something»: collecting.

questions.stem: (A) Neither the author (B) or the editor (C) noticed (D) the inconsistency.
questions.explanation: «Neither» se empareja con «nor», no con «or».

questions.stem: (A) The lecture was (B) so interesting (C) lecture that (D) nobody left early.
questions.explanation: Sobra «lecture»: «so interesting that» o «such an interesting lecture that».

questions.stem: (A) Most researchers agree (B) that the model (C) needs revising, (D) but few has proposed alternatives.
questions.explanation: «Few» es plural: few have proposed.

questions.stem: (A) The device consists (B) in three parts, (C) each of which (D) can be replaced separately.
questions.explanation: «Consist of», no «consist in» en este sentido.

parts.title: Texto 1
parts.instructions: Lee el texto y responde a las preguntas.
parts.passage:
The acoustics of ancient Greek theatres have been the subject of a persistent legend: that a whisper on the stage can be heard in the last row. Measurements taken at Epidaurus show that the claim is exaggerated but not baseless.

What the seating actually does is filter. The rows of stone form a regular corrugated surface, and such surfaces reflect low frequencies poorly while returning higher ones towards the audience. Since the background noise of an outdoor crowd is concentrated at low frequencies, the effect is to suppress the noise relative to the voice.

The voice itself is not amplified. A speaker at the centre is not louder in absolute terms at the back; the speech is simply less masked by everything else.

Whether the Greeks understood this is doubtful. The geometry that produces the effect follows from building a steep semicircle in stone, which is what the site and the materials suggested anyway. Later theatres built on the same plan in different materials do not perform as well, which indicates that the acoustic result was a consequence of the design rather than its purpose.

questions.stem: What is the main idea of the passage?
options: Greek theatres amplified the human voice.
The acoustic effect is real but works by filtering noise.
The legend about whispers is entirely false.
questions.explanation: El texto explica que filtra ruido, no que amplifique.

questions.stem: What does the seating do to low frequencies?
questions.explanation: Segundo párrafo.

questions.stem: Why does this help the audience?
options: Crowd noise is mostly low frequency.
questions.explanation: El ruido de fondo se concentra en frecuencias bajas.

questions.stem: The word «masked» in paragraph 3 is closest in meaning to
questions.explanation: El habla queda menos tapada por el ruido.

questions.stem: According to the passage, is the voice amplified?
options: No, it is not louder in absolute terms.
questions.explanation: Tercer párrafo, explícito.

questions.stem: What suggests the effect was unintentional?
options: Later theatres in other materials perform worse.
questions.explanation: Último párrafo.

questions.stem: The word «corrugated» in paragraph 2 is closest in meaning to
questions.explanation: Superficie con surcos regulares, como las filas de asientos.

questions.stem: It can be inferred that the legend persists because
questions.explanation: «exaggerated but not baseless».

questions.stem: What determined the steep semicircular shape?
questions.explanation: Último párrafo.

questions.stem: The author's attitude towards the legend is best described as
questions.explanation: Lo matiza: exagerado pero con base real.

parts.title: Texto 2
parts.instructions: Lee el texto y responde a las preguntas.
parts.passage:
Antibiotic resistance is often described as bacteria becoming stronger, which misrepresents the process. Resistance is not acquired by individual bacteria during treatment; it is present beforehand in a small fraction of the population, and treatment removes everything else.

This matters for how the problem should be addressed. If resistance were caused by exposure, then reducing the dose would reduce the risk. Because resistance is selected rather than induced, the opposite is closer to the truth: incomplete treatment leaves precisely the resistant fraction alive and removes its competitors.

The resistant survivors are not necessarily fitter in other respects. Resistance frequently carries a metabolic cost, which is why resistant strains tend to decline when the antibiotic is withdrawn. In the absence of the drug, they are outcompeted by ordinary bacteria.

This has led to proposals for cycling antibiotics at the level of an entire hospital, allowing resistant strains to fade before the drug is reintroduced. Results have been mixed. The strategy assumes the cost of resistance is high enough to matter within months, and for several important organisms it is not.

questions.stem: What common description does the author reject?
options: That bacteria become stronger during treatment.
questions.explanation: Primera frase.

questions.stem: According to the passage, where does resistance come from?
options: It is caused by high doses.
It is already present in a small fraction.
It is induced by the drug.
questions.explanation: Primer párrafo.

questions.stem: Why is incomplete treatment dangerous?
options: It leaves the resistant fraction without competitors.
questions.explanation: Segundo párrafo, explícito.

questions.stem: The word «selected» in paragraph 2 is closest in meaning to
questions.explanation: Selección: sobreviven los que ya eran resistentes.

questions.stem: Why do resistant strains often decline when the drug is withdrawn?
questions.explanation: Tercer párrafo.

questions.stem: What is the cycling strategy?
questions.explanation: Cuarto párrafo.

questions.stem: What assumption does that strategy rely on?
options: That resistance costs enough to matter within months.
questions.explanation: Última frase.

questions.stem: The phrase «results have been mixed» suggests the strategy
questions.explanation: Resultados desiguales.

questions.stem: It can be inferred that reducing the dose would
options: not solve the problem and may worsen it.
questions.explanation: El texto dice que lo contrario está más cerca de la verdad.

questions.stem: The word «outcompeted» in paragraph 3 is closest in meaning to
questions.explanation: Las bacterias normales les ganan.

parts.title: Texto 3
parts.instructions: Lee el texto y responde a las preguntas.
parts.passage:
The global trade in second-hand clothing is larger than most people assume and operates on a logic that is frequently misunderstood. Garments donated in wealthy countries are rarely distributed free of charge. They are sorted, graded and sold in bulk to importers, who resell them in local markets.

Critics argue that this trade undermines domestic textile industries in the importing countries, and there is evidence for the claim in several African markets during the 1980s and 1990s. Supporters point out that the same trade employs large numbers of people in sorting, transport and retail, and supplies clothing at prices that local manufacture could not match.

Both positions are usually stated as though the effect were uniform, which it is not. Where a domestic industry already existed, imports competed with it directly. Where none existed, the trade created a distribution network without displacing anything.

A further complication is that only a fraction of donated clothing is sellable. Estimates vary widely, but a substantial proportion is unusable and becomes waste in the destination country, which now carries a disposal cost that the donor country avoided. That transfer rarely appears in either side of the argument.

parts.title: Texto 4
parts.instructions: Lee el texto y responde a las preguntas.
parts.passage:
Lightning is commonly imagined as a single flash travelling from cloud to ground, but the sequence is more complicated and runs partly in the opposite direction. A faint channel of ionised air, called the stepped leader, descends from the cloud in a series of short jumps, branching as it goes.

When the leader approaches the surface, objects below send up shorter channels of their own. The first of these to meet the descending leader completes the circuit, and the visible flash, the return stroke, travels upward along the established path.

This explains why the branches of a lightning bolt point downward in photographs even though the bright stroke moves up: the branches were made by the invisible leader on its way down, and only the successful path is illuminated.

It also explains why tall objects are struck more often without being the cause of the strike. The leader does not aim at anything. It descends by a path determined by local conditions, and only in the final tens of metres does the height of a structure decide which upward channel connects first. A lightning rod does not attract lightning from a distance; it simply wins a very short race.

parts.title: Texto 5
parts.instructions: Lee el texto y responde a las preguntas.
parts.passage:
The reintroduction of a predator into an ecosystem is often presented as restoring a balance, a phrase that carries assumptions worth examining. Balance implies a single stable state to which the system returns, and ecosystems rarely behave that way.

The best-documented case is the return of wolves to a large national park in the 1990s. Elk numbers fell, young trees recovered along river valleys, and the rivers themselves changed course less often as the banks stabilised. The account is accurate as far as it goes.

What is usually omitted is that other changes occurred at the same time. A prolonged drought ended, hunting regulations outside the park changed, and a bear population was recovering independently. Attributing the vegetation recovery entirely to wolves requires ignoring three simultaneous causes.

Ecologists working on the site have been considerably more careful than the popular accounts. Their estimates of the wolf contribution range from substantial to modest, and the disagreement is not a sign of a failing field. It reflects the difficulty of isolating one variable in a system where nothing can be held constant and no control site exists.
